value.rules_markdown:
- One responsibility per module, with core types in a module-local `types.rs`.
- Every port in `src/ports/` is one trait in one file.
- Declare every CLI subcommand even when its milestone has not landed.
- Production surface lives only in `src/server/`; do not distribute or run as a GitHub Action.
- Add review policies as data folders under `presets/`, never as new code modules.
- Never edit the `vendor/tinyagents` submodule; change it upstream and bump the pin.
- Declare examples in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential-needing tests skip in CI.
- Keep the default build offline; network needs go behind features (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Use rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` for modules/files, `PascalCase` for types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Start every file with a `//!` module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; note why load-bearing flags or orderings matter.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` so it becomes help text.
- Keep tests in-crate as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, moving to sibling `test.rs` when large; no `tests/` directory.
- Give every port an always-compiled offline mock.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests asserting findings after filtering, dedupe and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep Markdown files at 500 lines or fewer; split and link when larger.
- The model never holds a write token; lanes run read-only and write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/` after model calls.
- Never execute contributor code; read diff and tree only.
- Treat PR bodies, comments and diffs as untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts.
- Only deterministic policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub; model verdicts are advisory.
- Report found secrets by type and location only; never expose the value in comments, summaries or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects and keep commits small.
- PRs state what changed, behaviour changes, and how it was verified.
